analysis.investment_thesis: Anand Rathi Wealth is a genuinely exceptional asset-light business — ROCE of 59.2% and 31.6% net profit CAGR over 7 years are rare — but the Magic Formula demands both quality AND cheapness, and the market has priced out every last rupee of margin of safety. At an earnings yield of roughly 1.6% (EBIT ~INR 482 Cr / EV ~INR 30,475 Cr) and P/E of 77x, you are paying a luxury-goods price for a financial-services business.
key_strengths: Exceptional capital efficiency: ROCE 59.2%, ROE 47.3%, operating margin 40%+ in a fee-based, asset-light wealth management model
Consistent compounding: net profit grew at 31.6% CAGR over 7 years with 5/5 years of positive OCF
Minimal debt (D/E 0.08) and growing cash position (INR 241 Cr in 2026), funding growth entirely from operations
key_risks: Market-linked revenue: a sustained equity bear market could cut AUM-based fees sharply and compress margins
Extreme valuation — at 77x P/E any earnings deceleration will cause severe multiple compression
Financial company structurally excluded from Magic Formula; EBIT/EV of ~1.6% offers zero margin of safety by any earnings-yield framework
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~1.6% is one of the worst in any universe I screen — Magic Formula requires 12%+ to even enter consideration
Other income jumped to INR 105 Cr in 2026 from near-zero previously — possible one-time item inflating reported profits
Financial company: capital structure and leverage distort Magic Formula metrics; excluded from valid ROIC ranking
analysis.detailed_analysis: By the Magic Formula, this stock fails categorically on valuation. Enterprise value of roughly INR 30,475 Cr against EBIT of INR 482 Cr yields an earnings yield of ~1.6%, far below the 12% minimum I require and the 15%+ that signals real value. The business itself is extraordinary — an asset-light, high-ROCE wealth manager serving HNI and UHNI clients with an expanding technology platform — but the formula ranks stocks on BOTH axes simultaneously, and a poor earnings yield disqualifies even the finest business. The 2026 'Other Income' spike of INR 105 Cr (vs. near-zero historically) warrants scrutiny before accepting the reported net profit of INR 397 Cr at face value.
